title: The Cyber Threat Landscape for Financial Services
summary: The threat actors, attack vectors and sector-specific vulnerabilities facing regulated firms and market infrastructure, and how threat intelligence should shape supervisory priorities.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The threat actors, attack vectors and sector-specific vulnerabilities facing regulated firms and market infrastructure, and how threat intelligence should shape supervisory priorities.
Learning Objectives: Explain the main categories of cyber threat actor and their motivations
Identify sector-specific vulnerabilities in payments, trading, custody and core systems
Assess how threat intelligence should inform supervisory priorities
Syllabus: Threat actors: nation-state, organised crime, insiders and opportunists
Attack vectors: phishing, ransomware, supply chain compromise and data extortion
Legacy systems and technical debt as vulnerability drivers
Sources and supervisory use of threat intelligence
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors assessing operational resilience, ICT and cyber risk across banking, insurance, investment, payments and market infrastructure
Technology risk, cyber and outsourcing specialists supporting supervisory teams
Policy staff and senior managers shaping the authority's resilience, cyber and critical third-party approach
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision or operational risk is helpful. No technical background in IT or cybersecurity is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for Operational Resilience (2021)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
FSB, Effective Practices for Cyber Incident Response and Recovery (2020)
